hints.title: Cost Partitioning
hints.text: For each chocolate with price p, the relative loss is p if p <= k, and 2*k - p if p > k.

hints.title: Sorted Greedy Partition
hints.text: Sort the prices array and compute prefix sums. To minimize relative loss, pick small prices <= k from the left and large prices > k from the right.

hints.title: Binary Search Split Boundary
hints.text: Use binary search to find the optimal number of items l taken from the left such that prices[mid] < 2 * k - prices[n - (m - mid)].

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def minimumRelativeLosses(self, prices: List[int], queries: List[List[int]]) -> List[int]:
        from bisect import bisect_right
        from itertools import accumulate
        prices.sort()
        s = list(accumulate(prices, initial=0))
        n = len(prices)
        def f(k: int, m: int) -> int:
            l, r = 0, min(m, bisect_right(prices, k))
            while l < r:
                mid = (l + r) >> 1
                right = m - mid
                if prices[mid] < 2 * k - prices[n - right]:
                    l = mid + 1
                else:
                    r = mid
            return l
        ans = []
        for k, m in queries:
            l = f(k, m)
            r = m - l
            loss = s[l] + 2 * k * r - (s[n] - s[n - r])
            ans.append(loss)
        return ans
```

complexity.time: O(n log n + q log m)
complexity.notes: Prefix sum precomputation with binary search on the optimal prefix count.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating all combinations of m chocolates per query takes exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(n) auxiliary prefix sums enable constant time range queries.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use binary search on the monotonic marginal contribution condition.
